# SHYFEM Full-Codebase Deep Review — 2026-07-18

**Scope:** entire repository — Fortran model core, MPI layer, ecological models, Fortran/C tools, build system, and the Python Shiny UI (`shyfem-ui`).
**Baseline:** the 2026-06-20 deep review (54 findings). Finders were instructed to find *new* issues only; a separate track verified remediation status of every prior finding.

---

## 1. Executive summary

The headline discovery is self-inflicted: **this fork's own performance remediations introduced a family of OpenMP data races in the scalar-transport core**. Commits `34ff6dd` and `38469ab` converted per-call work arrays to `allocatable, save` ("allocation caching") in `conz3d_omp`, `scal_adv`, and `conzstab` — but `save` locals are *shared* across OpenMP tasks, and these routines run concurrently from sibling tasks (`barocl` + `tracer_compute` under the PARALLEL/SINGLE region in `shyfem_subs.f90:1009-1033`). The result is 1 critical + 3 high findings: in a default OMP build with `ibarcl>0` and `iconz>=1`, temperature/salinity and tracer fields are silently corrupted (or the run crashes on double-alloc/dealloc). A fourth high finding in the same area: MPI calls are issued from inside those concurrent tasks, violating the `MPI_THREAD_FUNNELED` contract of the hybrid build. **The "allocation caching" pattern documented in CLAUDE.md is only safe in routines never called concurrently — it must not be applied inside OMP task regions without `!$OMP THREADPRIVATE` or per-thread arrays.**

Other top-tier confirmed findings: **PETSc/AmgX solves never check convergence** (`KSPGetConvergedReason` is absent from the codebase — a diverged solve silently becomes the free surface, where SPARSKIT would stop hard); **femtime's fossil `it` is frozen at `itanf`**, silently disabling lagrangian decay/mortality/connectivity; **`make petsc` delivers a SPARSKIT binary** due to symlink bit-rot; wind-stress input divides by zero at calm points; `proj_geo2cart` uses half-range instead of midpoint as the projection reference, distorting all derived cartesian distances; and in the UI, **job cancellation never terminates the spawned `shyfem`/`mpirun` process** and **any WebSocket disconnect auto-cancels running jobs** — plus `init_db`'s Alembic branch is dead code (wrong `alembic.ini` path), so fresh installs never run migrations/stamping.

The remediation scoreboard is honest but sobering: of the 54 June findings, **16 are fixed and 4 partial — all 6 of the June high-priority items (F01–F06) are fixed** — but 34 remain open, concentrated in the deliberately-deferred tail: bare `stop`s in MPI paths (F07/F09/F11/F27/F38), mercury-model hygiene (F09/F10/F31), C-tool memory safety (F12/F39/F40/F43), MPI hygiene (F32–F34), and UI low-tier items. One regression came from the HEAD remediation commit itself: switching the MPI debug file to `newunit=` yields a negative unit number, silently disabling every `my_unit>0` debug guard.

**Fresh confirmed findings: 54** (original severities: 1 critical / 14 high / 39 medium; verifier-adjusted: 13 high / 31 medium / 10 low — downgrades annotated inline). 16 candidate findings were refuted by adversarial verification (§5). 46 low-tier findings are reported unverified (§4).

### 2.1 Critical & high — details

#### N01 · CRITICAL (adj. high) · conz3d_omp save-cached work arrays are shared across concurrent scalar tasks and deallocated mid-use
**Location:** `src/shyfem/concentration_omp.f90:173` · **Area:** Scalar transport (OMP/TVD) · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED

Commit 38469ab added `save` to the five allocatable work arrays cn/co/cdiag/clow/chigh (lines 173-177) and wrapped allocation in lazy-init guards (195-214), but left the DEALLOCATE calls at the end of the routine (353-357). conz3d_omp is invoked concurrently from independent OMP tasks: shyfem_subs.f90:1009-1033 runs `barocl(1)` (temp/salt via scal_adv_nudge -> scal3sh -> conz3d_omp) and `tracer_compute` (each tracer via scal_adv, itself spawning nested tasks at conz_admin.f90:451) as sibling tasks inside a PARALLEL/SINGLE region. Two concurrent calls now share one saved array set: the second caller sees allocated(cn)=.true., skips allocation, and zeroes/overwrites the first caller's in-progress accumulation; the first caller then DEALLOCATEs the arrays while the second is still using them. Before 38469ab the arrays were per-call allocatables and thread-safe; the 'caching' also gains nothing because the arrays are still deallocated every call.

**Failure scenario:** Default OMP build (`make fem`), STR with ibarcl>0 and iconz>=1, OMP_NUM_THREADS>=2: every timestep the temp task and a tracer task enter conz3d_omp concurrently; temperature and tracer contributions are accumulated into the same cn/cdiag arrays producing scientifically wrong T/S and tracer fields, and/or the run aborts with 'Attempt to DEALLOCATE unallocated' or segfaults on use-after-free when one task deallocates under the other.

#### N02 · HIGH · make petsc delivers a shyfem-petsc that is actually the SPARSKIT binary
**Location:** `Makefile:149` · **Area:** Build system & scripts · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED

bin/shyfem is not a regular file but an absolute symlink to src/shyfem/shyfem (created by src/shyfem/Makefile's `links` target via bin/symlink: `ln -fs $actdir/$file`; verified on disk: `bin/shyfem -> /home/razinka/shyfem/src/shyfem/shyfem`). The petsc recipe does `mv bin/shyfem bin/shyfem-petsc`, which renames the symlink, not the binary. It then runs `cd src/shyfem; make clean` (which deletes src/shyfem/shyfem, the symlink's target) and `cd src; make` (which rebuilds src/shyfem/shyfem with the default SPARSKIT solver and re-creates the bin/shyfem link). Both bin/shyfem and bin/shyfem-petsc now dereference to the same freshly built SPARSKIT binary; the PETSc build is destroyed. The recipe then prints "Both solvers ready: bin/shyfem (SPARSKIT) and bin/shyfem-petsc (PETSc)" and exits 0. The shyfem-ui solver dropdown routes PETSc jobs to bin/shyfem-petsc, so users selecting PETSc silently run SPARSKIT. Fix requires copying the dereferenced binary (e.g. `cp -L` or moving src/shyfem/shyfem itself) before the clean/rebuild.

**Failure scenario:** User runs `make petsc` (PETSC_DIR set correctly, PETSc build succeeds). Target exits 0 announcing both solvers ready. `bin/shyfem-petsc mm_hyd_00.str` — or a UI job with solver=PETSc — executes the SPARSKIT solver. Any PETSc-specific validation, benchmark, or bug reproduction (e.g. for the known F04 double-assembly issue) silently tests the wrong solver and reports wrong conclusions.

#### N03 · HIGH · Wind-stress input (iwtype=2): division by zero wspeed at calm points
**Location:** `src/shyfem/meteo_forcing.f90:924` · **Area:** Forcing & boundary conditions · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED

In meteo_convert_wind_data's bstress branch: `wspeed = sqrt(txy/(cd*wfact*roluft))` then `wx(k) = tx(k) / (cd*wspeed)` and `wy(k) = ty(k) / (cd*wspeed)` (lines 922-925) with no guard on txy==0. If a node has zero stress, wspeed=0 and the division is 0/0. The default NORMAL build profile compiles with `-ffpe-trap=zero,invalid,overflow` (Rules.make:708), so this raises SIGFPE and kills the run; under SPEED profile it yields NaN wx/wy that propagate to wave coupling and output.

**Failure scenario:** A wstress-type wind file (iwtype=2) containing a calm point (taux=tauy=0 — common in real stress fields or land-masked cells zero-filled) -> 0/0 at that node -> SIGFPE crash in the default build, or silent NaN wind components in optimized builds.

#### N04 · HIGH · KSPSolve convergence never checked - diverged PETSc/AmgX solves silently accepted as zeta
**Location:** `src/shyfem/mod_petsc_system.f90:602` · **Area:** Hydrodynamics & solvers · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED

solve_PETSc calls KSPSolve and checks only the PETSc error code perr, which is 0 even when the Krylov solver diverges (KSPGetConvergedReason / KSPSetErrorIfNotConverged are never used anywhere in the PETSc integration; confirmed by grep). solve_AmgX (lines 631-633) likewise ignores the solver status entirely. On non-convergence, X holds the last (garbage or stagnated) iterate, get_solution copies it into znv, and the simulation continues with no diagnostic. This breaks behavioral parity with the SPARSKIT backend, which stops hard on solver failure (sparskit_admin.f90:329-332). KSPSetTolerances leaves maxits at default and the hard-coded GMRES(default restart)+PCBJACOBI setup has no fallback.

**Failure scenario:** MPI+PETSc run (the configuration the Solver UI routes large meshes to) with extensive wetting/drying: hydro_zeta replaces dry-element rows with pure Laplacian blocks (hydrodynamic.f90:855-872), producing an ill-conditioned/near-singular system; restarted GMRES stagnates or breaks down, KSPSolve still returns perr=0, and a wrong free surface is committed to znv every step -> transports, volumes and all tracers drift with zero warnings, while the same run under SPARSKIT would stop with an explicit solver error.

#### N05 · HIGH · femtime `it` frozen at itanf (and `itend` never set) silently breaks lagrangian decay, mortality and connectivity
**Location:** `src/shyfem/time_admin.f90:703` · **Area:** Main loop & restart · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED

setup_time sets `it = itanf` (time_admin.f90:360) once; the update in set_timestep is commented out (`!it = t_act`, line 703) and `!itend = nint(dtend)` is commented at line 359, so the femtime module variables `it` and `itend` are never advanced/initialized during the run (verified: the only assignments to femtime `it` in the whole tree are time_admin.f90:360 and a local shadow in custom_admin.f90). But live physics still reads them: lagrange_decay.f90:107,152,181,225 compute particle age as `it - lgr_ar(i)%init%time`, while release times are set from the advancing clock `t_act` (lagrange_inout.f90:121). lagrange_connect.f90:227 gates connectivity-matrix output on `mod(it,itout)==0 .or. it==itend` with uninitialized `itend`. split_equal (time_admin.f90:791) also always passes its macro-step gate `mod(it-itanf,idtorig)==0`, recomputing the split every substep.

**Failure scenario:** Run the lagrangian module with ldecay>0 (or lcust=1/2/3): particle age = itanf - release_time <= 0 for every particle, so exp(-age/ldecay) >= 1 and the survival test never removes a particle — decay/mortality is silently a no-op and results (particle counts, connectivity, residence estimates) are wrong with no warning. lagr_conc returns immediately for all particles (lagrange_decay.f90:179). With itanf=0 (common relative-time setups), mod(0,itout)==0 makes the connectivity matrix rewrite every single timestep.

#### N06 · HIGH (adj. low) · InterpolateDepth dereferences NULL element on out-of-coverage centroid (supported workflow)
**Location:** `src/tools/mesh/intgrd.c:289` · **Area:** C tools · **Verdict:** PLAUSIBLE

ManipulateGrd (intgrd.c:131-133) does ped=FindElement(GD,xm,ym); pe->depth=DepthFromElement(ped) (which guards ped==NULL and returns NULLDEPTH) but then immediately overwrites that result with pe->depth=InterpolateDepth(GD,ped,xm,ym). InterpolateDepth (line 289: n=pe->vertex; and 294: pn=RetrieveByNodeNumber(G->HN,ind[i])) does NOT guard ped==NULL, so it dereferences a NULL Elem_type. FindElement returns NULL (line 233) whenever the target-mesh element centroid lies outside every source-grid element. The asymmetric NULL handling (DepthFromElement guards, InterpolateDepth does not, and the guarded result is discarded) confirms this is a bug. Secondary: InterpolateDepth uses float d[3] (line 287) filled by for(i=0;i<n;i++) with n=pe->vertex (293-296), so a source element with 4+ vertices writes d[3..] out of bounds.

**Failure scenario:** Run intgrd depth-grid new-grid to interpolate a bathymetry grid GD onto a model mesh GN (the tool's sole purpose). Any GN element whose centroid falls outside GD's coverage - domain boundaries, interior holes, mismatched extents, all routine in practice - makes FindElement return NULL and InterpolateDepth SIGSEGVs on pe->vertex.

#### N07 · HIGH · femelab -write/-condense use per-variable lmax as array leading dimension, mis-striding mixed 2D/3D FEM files
**Location:** `src/tools/shyelab/femelab1.f90:937` · **Area:** Fortran tools · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED

fem_file_read_data returns a per-record lmax into llmax(iv), which can be smaller than the file-level lmax (=nlvdi, the true leading dimension of data). write_minmax (line 937) calls minmax_data(l,llmax(iv),np,...,data(1,1,iv),...) so the dummy is declared data(llmax(iv),np) while the actual slab has stride nlvdi; likewise fem_condense is called at lines 583-585 with lmax_prof=llmax(iv) but dummy data(lmax,np) (declared at 1375-1382). For a 2D variable (llmax=1) in a 3D file, element (1,k) of the dummy maps to flat offset k, i.e. all levels of the first np/nlvdi nodes: statistics/averages are computed over a small subset of nodes, with flagged deep levels silently skipped. Such mixed files are standard: shyelab's own fem output (fem_write_hydro, shyelab_output.f90:700-726) writes zeta with lmax=1 and velocities with lmax=nlv.

**Failure scenario:** `shyelab -outformat fem hydro.shy` then `femelab -write out.fem`: zeta min/aver/max are computed over only ~np/nlv of the nodes (wrong extremes/means written to zeta 2d files and the terminal); `femelab -condense out.fem` writes an out.fem/out.txt where the condensed 2D variables are averages of the wrong memory locations - silently wrong converted data.

#### N08 · HIGH (adj. medium) · shyelab -vorticity writes nodal data as an element record (stale belem) and silently writes nothing for fem/gis/nc
**Location:** `src/tools/shyelab/shyelab1.f90:554` · **Area:** Fortran tools · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED

In the vorticity block (shyelab1.f90:550-557) the call to shyelab_record_output passes `belem` and `lmax` left over from the per-variable loop (line 487 sets belem=(bhydro .and. iv>1), so after the loop belem=.true. for the hydro files -vorticity requires). Vorticity is computed on nodes (compute_vorticity fills cv3(:,1:nkn)), but shy_write_output_record (src/utils/shyutilmpi/shy_util.f90:1031-1034) uses belem to set nn=nel_global and allocates cg(ng,nel_global) while cl is (nl,nkn); with bmpi_skip (single-rank shyelab) shympi_l2g_array executes the nonconforming assignment `val_out = vals` (mpi_node.f90), which is undefined behavior: out-of-bounds read of cl or a partially-filled element-sized record of a nodal field written into out.shy. For -outformat fem/gis/nc, shyelab_output.f90:347 (`if( bhydro .and. .not. bshy ) return`, keyed on the INPUT file type) returns before writing anything, yet shyelab_final_output still prints 'output written to out.fem'.

**Failure scenario:** `shyelab -vorticity -outformat shy hydro.shy` -> out.shy contains a record declared as nel elements filled from an nkn-sized nodal array (garbage/zero tail, possible OOB read crash under bounds checking); `shyelab -vorticity -outformat fem hydro.shy` -> empty out.fem while the tool reports success, so users get no data or corrupted vorticity fields.

#### N09 · HIGH · scal_adv save-cached boundary-condition arrays are shared across concurrent tracer tasks
**Location:** `src/shyfem/concentration.f90:298` · **Area:** Scalar transport (OMP/TVD) · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED

Commit 34ff6dd changed r3v/load/cobs/rtauv/wsinkv in scal_adv from per-call allocatables to `allocatable, save` with an unprotected lazy-init guard (lines 298-321). tracer_compute_multi (conz_admin.f90:446-475) runs scal_adv for each tracer i in its own OMP TASK; with iconz>=2 those tasks execute concurrently and share one r3v. Each task zeroes r3v (line 325) and then bnds_trans_new fills it with its own tracer's boundary values (350-351) while scal3sh re-reads r3v every substep via make_scal_flux (line 744), so a tracer can be advected with another tracer's (or zeroed) boundary concentrations. The first-timestep `if(.not.allocated(r3v)) allocate(...)` check is also racy: two tasks can both pass the test and the second allocate aborts at runtime. The same 34ff6dd pattern exists in scal_adv_nudge (397-413) and scal_adv_fact (486-502), currently exercised sequentially.

**Failure scenario:** OMP build, iconz=2 tracers with different open-boundary concentrations: task for tracer 1 fills r3v, then task for tracer 2 zeroes/refills it before tracer 1's scal3sh substeps read it; tracer 1 silently receives tracer 2's boundary mass input (wrong plumes near boundaries, no diagnostic). Alternatively both tasks allocate r3v on the first timestep and the run aborts with 'Attempting to allocate already allocated variable'.

#### N10 · HIGH · conzstab save-cached accumulation arrays race between concurrent stability checks, corrupting istot
**Location:** `src/shyfem/concentration.f90:1722` · **Area:** Scalar transport (OMP/TVD) · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED

Commit 34ff6dd made conzstab's cn/co/cdiag/clow/chigh/cwrite/c2write `allocatable, save` ('cached with save to avoid per-timestep allocation', lines 1722-1728, allocated once at 1765-1772 and retained). conzstab is called via scal3sh -> scalar_stability -> scalar_compute_stability (stability.f90:168) at the start of every scalar advection, i.e. concurrently from the barocl task and tracer tasks (shyfem_subs.f90:1016-1022, conz_admin.f90:451). Concurrent calls interleave the zeroing loop (1842-1854) with each other's element accumulation (1877-2051), so the stability sums voltot/flxtot (2076-2077) mix data from two scalars mid-zeroing. The resulting stabind/istot (2118-2120) controls the number of advection substeps in scal3sh.

**Failure scenario:** OMP run with temp/salt plus a tracer: the conz task zeroes cdiag while the temp task is accumulating volumes; stabind is underestimated, scal3sh runs with istot too small, the explicit advection violates its CFL bound and T/S develop oscillations/NaN (caught as SIGFPE in the trapping build, silent garbage in the SPEED profile). Overestimation instead can trip 'istot index too high' and stop the run.

#### N11 · HIGH · MPI exchanges and reductions issued from concurrent OMP tasks violate MPI_THREAD_FUNNELED and de-synchronize collective order
**Location:** `src/shyfem/concentration.f90:778` · **Area:** Scalar transport (OMP/TVD) · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED

shympi is initialized with MPI_THREAD_FUNNELED only (mpi_node_internal.f90:212), which forbids MPI calls from non-master threads. Yet in hybrid MPI+OMP builds the scalar tasks make MPI calls from task context: scal3sh calls shympi_exchange_3d_node twice per substep (concentration.f90:778,783), conzstab calls shympi_max five times (2099-2107), massconc calls shympi_sum (2192) from inside a tracer task (conz_admin.f90:469), and with itvd=2 conz3d_omp calls tvd_mpi_run point-to-point exchanges (concentration_omp.f90:245) and exchange_and_sum (305-311). Task scheduling order is nondeterministic per rank, so rank A's temp-task thread can enter a reduction while rank B's conz-task enters a different one; additionally the shared module buffers values_tvd_local/remote (mpi_tvd.f90:79-80) are overwritten per concurrent scalar.

**Failure scenario:** Hybrid build (MPI=true with OpenMP threads >1) running temp/salt plus tracers: two ranks execute the shympi_max/allreduce calls for different scalars in different order, pairing temperature's reduction with the tracer's on another rank — the run deadlocks in MPI or silently exchanges wrong halo/stability values between scalars; with itvd=2 the upwind-value buffers additionally deliver one scalar's remote values to another.

#### N12 · HIGH · init_db's Alembic branch is dead code: alembic.ini looked up at the wrong path, so migrations/stamping never run
**Location:** `shyfem-ui/shyfem_ui/db/base.py:97` · **Area:** UI data layer · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED

init_db() resolves ini_path = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "alembic.ini" = shyfem-ui/shyfem_ui/alembic.ini, but the file lives one level higher at shyfem-ui/alembic.ini (parents[2]; verified with ls and a path-resolution script; introduced in commit 45e0d82 which added alembic.ini only at the repo root). ini_path.exists() is therefore always False and init_db silently falls into the "installed package" create_all() fallback in every environment, including the git-checkout deployment on laguna. The docstring's promises — "For new databases, runs all migrations", "stamps the current head so future migrations apply cleanly" — are never fulfilled: command.upgrade/command.stamp at lines 104-119 are unreachable. create_all() only creates missing tables; it never ALTERs existing ones and never writes alembic_version. Consequences: (a) any existing DB upgraded via the app alone never receives new columns; (b) app-created DBs are unstamped, so a later manual `alembic upgrade head` starts from the base revision and fails on the first CREATE TABLE; (c) the stamp-vs-upgrade heuristic that was supposed to protect these DBs never executes. Fix is a one-character change (parents[2]), plus reconsidering the stamp heuristic (stamping head on a DB created by an older release's create_all would skip needed migrations).

**Failure scenario:** Operator has a v0.2.0-era shyfem_ui.db (no jobs.project_id, no feedbacks table), upgrades the code, and starts the app relying on init_db as documented. init_db runs create_all (no-op on existing tables) and returns cleanly; the first job submission then crashes with sqlite3.OperationalError "no such column: jobs.project_id" (or POST /api/feedback 500s with "no such table: feedbacks"). Alternatively: a fresh install creates the DB via app startup (create_all, unstamped); a later `alembic upgrade head` aborts with "table projects already exists" because the stamp branch that should have marked it never ran.

#### N13 · HIGH · Any WebSocket disconnect auto-cancels running jobs; local mode cancels ALL active jobs
**Location:** `shyfem-ui/shyfem_ui/services/job_queue.py:102` · **Area:** UI services · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED

cancel_active_jobs_for_session() is wired to session.on_ended (app.py:779). In local mode session_id is deliberately ignored (sid=None, line 102), so every session end cancels every active job — including jobs started from another still-open tab. In server mode jobs are tagged with the ephemeral str(id(session)) (related to known F17), so the owner's own disconnect cancels their jobs. Shiny has no reconnection: a page refresh, network blip, or laptop sleep ends the session. Combined with the notification logic (job_local.py:192-195, CANCELLED != COMPLETED -> notify_job_failed) the user also receives a spurious 'simulation failed' email, and per the wrapper bug the OS process actually keeps running.

**Failure scenario:** Local mode: user starts a 3-hour simulation, presses F5 to check another page — session ends, the job is marked cancelled and its work discarded. Server mode on laguna: user closes the laptop lid overnight expecting the server-side queue to finish the run; the WS drop cancels the job and sends a 'simulation failed' email, losing hours of computation.

#### N14 · HIGH · Job cancellation never terminates the spawned subprocess
**Location:** `shyfem-ui/shyfem_ui/services/shyfem_wrapper.py:204` · **Area:** UI services · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED

run_command() kills the child process only on asyncio.TimeoutError (line 207). Task cancellation (LocalJobQueue.cancel -> task.cancel() -> CancelledError raised inside 'await asyncio.wait_for(_drain_and_wait())') is caught by neither 'except asyncio.TimeoutError' nor 'except Exception' (CancelledError is BaseException), so it propagates to job_local.py:353 which marks the job CANCELLED — while the shyfem/mpirun process keeps running unsupervised. There is no finally: proc.kill(). The same leak occurs for any exception raised from output_callback (e.g. disk-full in write_output_line, job_local.py:29-31, which has no guard): 'except Exception' at line 220 returns a failed CommandResult with the process still alive.

**Failure scenario:** User cancels a 4-rank MPI simulation. UI shows CANCELLED and the semaphore slot is released, but mpirun keeps all ranks running for hours, burning CPU and writing .shy/.rst/.ext files. User fixes the STR and resubmits into the same working dir: two simulations now write the same output files concurrently, producing corrupted/interleaved results that downstream post-processing silently consumes.

#### N15 · HIGH · proj_geo2cart uses half-range instead of midpoint for projection reference point
**Location:** `src/utils/shyutilmpi/coordinates.f90:191` · **Area:** Generic utilities · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED

Lines 191-193 compute c_phi = 0.5*(ymax-ymin), c_lat0 = 0.5*(ymax-ymin), c_lon0 = 0.5*(xmax-xmin) - half the coordinate RANGE, not the basin center 0.5*(max+min). These are passed to init_coords/cpp_init (src/utils/generic/projection.f90:302-315), where xfact = yfact*cos(phi*rad) scales longitude to meters. For any spherical (lat/lon) basin the reference latitude becomes ~half the latitude span (typically 0.5-2 deg) instead of the central latitude, so xcartv east-west distances are stretched by cos(phi_wrong)/cos(lat_true) ~= 1/cos(lat). handle_projection is called unconditionally from shyfem_subs.f90:362, and xcartv/ycartv are consumed by baric_cart/getexy_cart in src/shyfem/waves_admin.f90:1576,1723 (wave fetch geometry).

**Failure scenario:** Spherical basin at 55N (e.g. Baltic lagoon grid) with the parametric wave module enabled: c_phi = 1 deg instead of 55 deg, cos(1)/cos(55) = 1.74, so every east-west fetch distance computed from xcartv is 74% too long -> systematically overestimated wave heights/periods in published results. At Venice latitude (45N) the error factor is 1.41.

### 2.2 Medium — details

- **N16 · Dockerfile cannot build against MPI-default Rules.make, and CMD references a nonexistent script** — `Dockerfile:29`
  Rules.make now defaults to PARALLEL_MPI = NODE (line 114) and PARTS = METIS / METISDIR = /usr (144-146), which makes F77 = mpif90 and links -lmetis. The builder stage installs only g++, gfortran, libxt-dev, libx11-dev, make (lines 13-19) — no OpenMPI, no libmetis-dev — so `RUN make clean && make fem` fails (with HEAD's check_mpi_vendor it now fails early with "mpif90 was not found"). Even if the build stage were fixed, the runtime stage (34-38) installs no MPI runtime (libmpi.so.40) so the binary could not start. Finally, CMD is `./examples/mar_menor/run.sh`: there is no `examples/` directory at the repo root (the case lives at testcases/examples/mar_menor) and no run.sh exists anywhere under it (only run_all.sh and mm_hyd_*.sh) — so even a successfully built image would fail at `docker run`. The Dockerfile has bit-rotted across both the source-tree restructure and the MPI-default switch.
  *Failure:* `docker build .` fails at the `make fem` layer with "ERROR: MPI build requested but mpif90 was not found". If someone patches only the package list, `docker run` then fails with "./examples/mar_menor/run.sh: No such file or directory" because neither the path nor the script exists in the image.

- **N17 · petsc target bypasses both check_mpi_vendor and the SOLVER=PETSC parameter validation (gap in the F13 fix)** — `Makefile:146`
  HEAD 73e03b2 added check_mpi_vendor as a prerequisite of `shyfem` only (line 143). The `petsc` target (line 146: `petsc: checkv libmod`) builds the same mpif90-linked binary but skips the vendor check, so the exact Intel-MPI silent-mislink scenario the fix targets (known F13) survives via `make petsc`. Additionally, `make petsc` passes SOLVER=PETSC only to the sub-make command line; the top-level `checkv` evaluates Rules.make with its file default SOLVER=SPARSKIT, so the PETSC_DIR-empty guard (Rules.make:454-459) never fires for this target. With PETSC_HOME unset, PETSC_DIR is empty and the sub-build proceeds with `-I/include` and `-L/lib -lpetsc_real`, dying with obscure compile/link errors instead of the intended "PETSC_DIR directory is empty" message. Reported as a new gap introduced/left by the F13 remediation, not a re-report of F13.
  *Failure:* On the dev box with Intel's mpif90 first in PATH, `make petsc` (no PATH=/usr/bin prefix) compiles and links cleanly against Intel MPI — no vendor error — and the resulting shyfem-petsc SIGFPEs inside MPI_Init at first run. Separately, a user without PETSC_HOME set runs `make petsc` and gets `f951: Warning: Nonexistent include directory '/include'` followed by `cannot find -lpetsc_real` rather than the designed configuration error.

- **N18 (adj. low) · make regress silently succeeds without running any tests; other advertised targets reference deleted legacy directories** — `Makefile:454`
  The regress recipe is `if [ -d $(REGRESSDIR) ]; then ...; fi` with REGRESSDIR=femregress. femregress does not exist in the restructured repo (verified), so `make regress` — advertised in help_dev as "runs regression tests (mpi for np>0)" — exits 0 having executed nothing. The same recipe also fails to export its SHYFEMDIR=$(PWD) assignment (plain shell variable, not exported), so even with a femregress checkout the child make would inherit the empty exported SHYFEMDIR from line 50 instead. Related rot: `nograph` (help: "compiles everything except graphics") depends only on checkv/directories/links/test_executable and compiles nothing — and test_executable/make_executable (lines 576-582) `chmod +x fembin/*` against the nonexistent fembin/. `compat` (line 522), `nompi` (566), `publish` (509), and rules_* helper text reference fem3d/fembin, all removed. FEMDIRS/FEMTOTS (lines 67-107) list only legacy directories, so `list` prints skip warnings for every entry.
  *Failure:* A developer or CI step runs `make regress` as a gate before merging; it returns exit 0 with no tests executed, and the pipeline goes green on completely unexercised code. A user following `make help`'s advice runs `make nograph` and gets `chmod: cannot access 'fembin/*'` — or, if fembin ever reappears, a successful exit having compiled nothing.

- **N19 · Documented build flags MPI=true/OMP=false are inert; no Makefile consumes them** — `Rules.make:114`
  CLAUDE.md and .github/workflows/fortran-ci.yml:89 both use `make fem OMP=false MPI=true PARTS=METIS METISDIR=/usr` as the canonical MPI build command, but a repo-wide search of every Makefile/*.make/*.mk (excluding src/external) finds zero references to $(MPI) or $(OMP). PARTS and METISDIR are real overrides; MPI and OMP are silently ignored. The build's parallelization is governed solely by PARALLEL_MPI (default NODE) and PARALLEL_OMP (default false) inside Rules.make. The commands only 'work' because the checked-in defaults happen to coincide with what the flags claim to request. There is no mapping (e.g. `ifeq ($(MPI),true) PARALLEL_MPI=NODE`) and no error for unknown command-line variables.
  *Failure:* A developer runs `make fem OMP=true` expecting an OpenMP build — they get PARALLEL_OMP=false, no -fopenmp compile flags on OMP regions, and a serial-threaded binary with no warning. Conversely `make fem MPI=false` still builds the MPI NODE binary. If the Rules.make default is ever flipped to PARALLEL_MPI=NONE, the CI job named 'MPI build' silently builds and green-lights a non-MPI binary while its command line still says MPI=true.

- **N20 · hersbach_cd (itdrag=5) unguarded for calm wind: log(0) and negative-base power** — `src/shyfem/meteo_forcing.f90:1653`
  hersbach_cd computes `R = (z/(am*nu))*(k*wxy)` and `A = (ach/(g_hersbach*z))*(k*wxy)**2` then takes log(R), log(A) (lines 1653-1656) with no lower bound on wxy. wxy=0 gives log(0) = -Inf (trapped as divide-by-zero under the default -ffpe-trap build); tiny nonzero wxy makes bnu = -1.47+0.93*log(R) negative, and `bnu**p` with double precision p=-12 evaluates as exp(p*log(bnu)) -> NaN. Compare heat_areg.f90:395 which clamps speed to 0.01 for exactly this reason. The 73e03b2 commit touched this routine (vonkarman import) without adding a guard.
  *Failure:* Run with itdrag=5 and any node with wind speed exactly 0 (calm cell, or a regular-grid hole filled with the wind vconst default of 0) -> SIGFPE in the default build or NaN drag coefficient -> NaN wind stress spreading through the momentum solution in SPEED builds.

- **N21 (adj. low) · has_waves() returns false for WW3 coupling (iwave=11/12), so turbulence ignores wave roughness** — `src/shyfem/waves_admin.f90:1829`
  has_waves() returns .true. only for 0 < iwave <= 5 (waves_admin.f90:1827-1835). WW3 coupling uses iwave=11/12 and getvarww3 actively computes wave-derived surface roughness z0sk = 0.5*Hs (ww3.f90:528). But gotm_shell caches `bwave = has_waves()` (turbulence.f90:350) and with bwave false uses the Charnock estimate instead of z0sk (turbulence.f90:478-481). The WW3-computed z0sk is therefore silently ignored in the GOTM surface boundary condition, inconsistent with WWM runs (iwave=2..5) where it is used.
  *Failure:* WW3-coupled run (iwave=11) with iturb=1/GOTM: surface mixing uses Charnock roughness instead of the wave-height-derived roughness the coupling computes, systematically underestimating wave-enhanced near-surface mixing — wrong vertical temperature/velocity structure with no warning.

- **N22 · set_advective ihwadv=1 reads ulov(0,ie)/vlov(0,ie) out of bounds at the surface layer** — `src/shyfem/explicit.f90:841`
  In the upwind vertical momentum advection branch, wtop is initialized to 0.0 per element, so at l=lmin the test if(wtop.gt.0.) is false and the else branch executes zxadv = wtop*ulov(l-1,ie) (lines 841-842). With lmin=1 (the normal case) this indexes ulov(0,ie)/vlov(0,ie); ulov/vlov are allocated (nlv,nel) 1-based (mod_hydro_vel.f90:87,91), so this is an out-of-bounds read on every element, every timestep, whenever ihwadv=1 and ilin=0.
  *Failure:* 3D run with nonlinear advection and ihwadv=1: for ie=1 the read precedes the array allocation; if the garbage bits form NaN/Inf, 0.0*NaN = NaN lands in fxv(1,1), the -ffpe-trap=invalid NORMAL build SIGFPEs or the SPEED build propagates NaN through hydro_intern into utlnv and the whole flow field. Any -fcheck=all (NOOPT/CHECK profile) build aborts deterministically at the first element, making the option undebuggable.

- **N23 · Explicit zeta scheme aborts on any wetting/drying event; bare stop in MPI collective context deadlocks** — `src/shyfem/simsys_spkaux.f90:643`
  When azpar/ampar are 0/1 or 1/0, hydro latches bsysexpl (hydrodynamic.f90:354-358) and system_assemble_omp takes the diagonal-only branch, which does stop 'error stop system_assemble_omp: non diag elems /= 0' whenever an off-diagonal entry is nonzero (line 643; same in system_assemble at 586). hydro_zeta unconditionally replaces dry-element (iwegv/=0) matrices with a Laplacian hh999*(b(n)*b(m)+c(n)*c(m)) that has generically nonzero off-diagonals (hydrodynamic.f90:744-762), so the first element that dries kills the run. The same latch also fires if setimp/changeimp temporarily forces implicit weights (iostr.f90:663-679) while bsysexpl remains permanently set. In MPI this is a bare stop on the assembling rank while the others wait in shympi_exchange_and_sum_2d_nodes / shympi_bcast -> deadlock (CLAUDE.md: no bare stop in MPI paths). Additionally the explicit solve divides rvec2d/raux2d without a zero guard (line 489).
  *Failure:* User runs the supported explicit configuration (azpar=0, ampar=1) on a basin with intertidal flats: at the first ebb that dries an element, a serial run aborts mid-simulation with a misleading 'non diag elems' message; an MPI run hangs forever consuming allocation until the scheduler kills it.

- **N24 · Restart read has no iostat past the first header record — a truncated final record aborts the run instead of falling back to the previous record** — `src/shyfem/restart.f90:937`
  rst_read_record guards only the 3-integer header with iostat (lines 900-907); every subsequent read — `read(iunit) nknaux,nelaux,nlvaux` (line 937), the flag reads, and all `read(iu) garray` in mod_restart.f90 restart_read_value_* (src/utils/shyutilmpi/mod_restart.f90:374,401,429,457,488) — is unguarded. rst_read_restart_file's blast mode (itrst=-1, 'use last record') reads sequentially until EOF, so it always walks into the final record. A restart file whose last record is partial is exactly what a crash/walltime-kill during rst_write_record produces (the writer appends multi-GB records with file_sync only after the full record, restart.f90:646).
  *Failure:* Cluster job dies mid-way through writing a restart record; user resubmits with itrst=-1 for crash recovery. Instead of using the last complete record (which is intact in the file), the run aborts with a Fortran runtime EOF error inside an unguarded read — the primary crash-recovery workflow fails and requires manual binary surgery or guessing an exact earlier itrst.

- **N25 · Restart round-trip silently drops model state: simple-sediment bed mass (hooks exist but unwired) and k-eps turbulence** — `src/shyfem/restart.f90:616`
  rst_write_record writes hydro/depth/T-S-rho/gotm/conz/wvert/eco/merc/bfm only. write_restart_ssedi/read_restart_ssedi/skip_restart_ssedi exist in src/shyfem/simple_sedi.f90:573-606 but are called from nowhere (verified by grep over the whole tree), so the accumulated bottom-sediment array conza [kg/m2] (enabled with issedi=1) restarts at its cold-start value of 0. Turbulence state is saved only for iturb==1 (GOTM, restart.f90:616-619); for iturb==2 the k-eps closure state tken/eps in mod_keps (turbulence.f90:1296,1324) is lost, as are visv/difv and z0bk, so the first steps after restart run with cold-start mixing.
  *Failure:* A long morphodynamic/deposition study with issedi=1 is run in yearly restart segments: at every restart the bed-mass field conza is silently reset to zero, so the final sediment accumulation budget is wrong (data loss), with no warning anywhere. An iturb=2 run restarted mid-storm re-develops turbulence from scratch, producing a mixing discontinuity relative to the uninterrupted run.

- **N26 · Vertical layer structure in restart file (hlv/ilhv/ilhkv) is read but never validated against the run; rst_get_vertical is dead code** — `src/shyfem/restart.f90:948`
  rst_read_record checks only the counts nkn/nel/nlv (lines 937-946). rst_read_vertical (lines 1084-1128) reads hlvrst/ilhrst/ilhkrst into module arrays, but nothing ever compares them with the run's hlv/ilhv/ilhkv — rst_get_vertical (line 1132) is never called from anywhere (verified by grep). The 'hlv not compatible' diagnostic is unreachable as a real hlv check: rst_read_restart_file maps ANY positive read error to ierr=94 (lines 313-316), which rst_perform_restart then reports as '*** hlv not compatible' (lines 224-227) even when the actual problem is a bad idfile magic (ierr=7).
  *Failure:* User changes the $levels section between runs keeping the same number of layers (e.g. refines spacing from 2 m to non-uniform with identical nlv): the restart is accepted silently and 3D T/S/velocity fields written on the old layer geometry are loaded onto the new one — vertically misplaced water masses and wrong stratification with no error or warning. Separately, a corrupt header makes the model claim 'hlv not compatible', sending the user to debug the wrong thing.

- **N27 · Restart writes have no iostat anywhere, and single-record mode overwrites the only record in place — a failed write destroys the sole recovery point** — `src/shyfem/restart.f90:516`
  rst_write_record's header writes (lines 588-593) and all restart_write_value_* routines (src/utils/shyutilmpi/mod_restart.f90:198-350) write without iostat/err handling. In bonce mode (idtrst<0, 'keep only last record'), rst_write_restart re-opens '.rst' each time with status 'new', which ifileo silently maps to 'unknown' (src/utils/generic/file.f90:163-169), truncating the existing file on the first write (restart.f90:512-521). The previous restart record is therefore destroyed before the new one is durably written, with no error checking during the write.
  *Failure:* Run with idtrst=-43200 (12-hourly single-record restart): the filesystem fills up (or the node dies) while the new record is being written — the old record has already been truncated away, the new one is partial, and the simulation now has zero usable restart points; combined with the unguarded read path the next itrst=-1 attempt aborts. A plain disk-full otherwise crashes the whole simulation with an unhandled Fortran I/O error rather than a controlled message.

- **N28 · Global-mesh-sized automatic stack arrays in MPI setup path (shympi_setup, transfer_domain, handle_partition) crash on large basins** — `src/utils/shympi/mpi_basin.f90:88`
  shympi_setup declares five automatic arrays sized by the still-global mesh: nodes(nkn), elems(nel), nindex(nkn), eindex(nel), area_node(nkn) (mpi_basin.f90:88-92); handle_partition adds area_elem(nel) (line 1130) on top while area_node is still on the caller's stack; transfer_domain adds inverse(nkn) with global nkn (line 765). gfortran places automatic arrays on the stack. The same pattern persists in the ghost-consistency check routines: shympi_check_3d_node_r uses automatic aux(nlvdi,nkn) (mpi_node.f90:1519) and shympi_check_3d0_node_r aux(0:nlvdi,nkn) (line 1542), although the sibling shympi_check_3d_elem_r was already converted to allocatable (lines 1626-1631), showing the fix was applied inconsistently. This is the exact stack-to-allocatable class the Phase-1 remediation claimed to close.
  *Failure:* MPI run on a large basin (e.g. 2M nodes / 4M elements): shympi_setup needs ~24MB (3 x 8MB nkn-arrays) + ~32MB (2 x 16MB nel-arrays) of stack in one frame; with the default 8MB ulimit -s every rank dies with SIGSEGV inside shympi_setup at startup, with no error message and no MPI_ABORT — mpirun reports only a signal 11, which is very hard to diagnose. Similarly, enabling the mpi_assert 3D node checks on a deep, large local domain (100k nodes x 60 levels = 24MB automatic aux) crashes the debug check itself.

- **N29 · newunit= makes my_unit negative, silently disabling all my_unit>0 MPI debug guards** — `src/utils/shympi/mpi_node.f90:693`
  The commit replaced `my_unit = my_unit_base + my_id` (800+rank, always positive) with `open(newunit=my_unit,...)`. Fortran 2008 requires NEWUNIT= to return a negative unit number (gfortran uses -10 and below). But the consumers of this module variable gate their output on positivity: mpi_ghost.f90:138 and :501 (`bdebug = ( my_unit > 0 )`) and mpi_basin.f90:163 and :180 (`if( my_unit > 0 ) then`). The author fixed the equivalent guard in shyfem_subs.f90 (`iunit > 0` -> `iunit /= 0`) but missed all my_unit consumers, so the ghost-area and domain-decomposition dumps are now silently skipped even when debugging is enabled.
  *Failure:* Developer sets bmpi_debug_txt=.true. and rebuilds to diagnose an MPI decomposition problem. mpi_debug_<rank>.txt files are created but contain only the 5-line init header from shympi_init; all ghost-node/ghost-elem info (mpi_ghost) and node/element domain listings (mpi_basin) are silently absent because my_unit is negative, defeating the commit's stated goal of improved MPI diagnostics.

- **N30 (adj. low) · sprintf("%f", coord/depth) into char s[20] overflows on large grd values** — `src/tools/grid/gridma2.c:272`

"%f" with default precision emits up to ~46 chars for large-magnitude floats; a coordinate or depth with >=13 integer digits already exceeds the 20-byte buffer including the ".000000" suffix and terminator. Result: first header says lmax=nz1, all data records and all subsequent headers say lmax=nz, and the 2header from record 2 onward writes hlv(1:nz) including the hlv(nz)=0 slot zeroed by depth_shift_up (non-monotone levels).

- **N37 · Sediment deposition feedback writes through an intent(in) dummy chain (undefined behavior)** — `src/shyfem/concentration_omp.f90:861`
  conz3d_nodes adjusts the load array for excess deposition: `if( rload > 0. ) load(l,k) = loading / rload` (line 861), with load declared intent(inout) here (807) and in conz3d_omp (150). But the actual argument arrives through scal3sh, where load is declared intent(in) (concentration.f90:603), and through scal_adv_fact, also intent(in) (concentration.f90:481). Modifying a nondefinable intent(in) dummy is a Fortran standard violation; it currently 'works' only because the arrays are passed by reference with no explicit interfaces between the files. A compiler is entitled to copy-in an intent(in) array or assume it unchanged across the call, in which case the clipped deposition rate is never returned to the cohesive-sediment module.
  *Failure:* Cohesive sediment run (scal_adv_fact with rload=1 and negative load = deposition): after LTO/aggressive optimization or a compiler that copies the intent(in) dummy, the sediment module keeps using the unclipped deposition rate while the water column was deposited less — bed mass and suspended mass silently diverge (mass budget error), with no warning.

- **N38 · decay_conz_chapra double-counts settling and transfers concentration between layers without thickness weighting** — `src/shyfem/conz_admin.f90:741`
  With idecay=2, each layer is first attenuated by exp(-dtt*kb) where kb already includes the settling rate kbs=fp*ws/h (lines 736-739). Then eflux_bottom = e*(1-exp(-dtt*kbs)) is subtracted again (740-741), so the settling loss is applied twice (net factor exp(-2*dtt*kbs)). Furthermore eflux_bottom is a concentration removed from layer l (thickness h_l) and added unchanged to layer l+1 (thickness h_{l+1}) via eflux_top (741-742); mass transferred is eflux*h_l*A but mass received is eflux*h_{l+1}*A, so inter-layer settling does not conserve tracer mass unless layers have equal thickness.
  *Failure:* A 3D run with idecay=2 and stretched vertical layers (thin surface, thick bottom): bacteria concentration decays roughly twice as fast as the Chapra formulation intends via the doubled kbs term, and each settling transfer into a thicker layer spuriously creates mass proportional to h_{l+1}/h_l — total tracer mass drifts systematically every timestep with no diagnostic.

It currently works only if the compiler happens to reuse the same stack slot with an unclobbered value between timesteps.
  *Failure:* Run with itsmed=1: between ts_shell calls other routines clobber the stack slot holding nr; at output time rr=1./nr uses a bogus count (e.g. huge, zero or negative), so the tsmed file's mean T/S records are scaled wrongly or become Inf — analysis products are silently corrupted while min/max records look plausible.

- **N45 (adj. low) · Login timing oracle enables username and active-status enumeration** — `shyfem-ui/shyfem_ui/services/auth_service.py:251`
  authenticate() returns immediately when the user does not exist (line 251-252) or is inactive (line 253-254), skipping the argon2 verify_password call entirely; only an existing, active account reaches the expensive argon2 verification (line 255). There is no dummy-hash comparison to equalize timing. The response HTML and audit action ('login_failed') are identical, but the ~50-100ms argon2 cost creates a large, network-measurable timing difference between (a) nonexistent/inactive usernames and (b) valid active usernames, giving an unauthenticated attacker a reliable username- and active-status-enumeration oracle. The 120 rpm/IP rate limit does not prevent statistical enumeration.
  *Failure:* Attacker POSTs /login with wrong passwords for candidate usernames and measures response latency: fast (~ms) responses reveal usernames that do not exist or are deactivated; slow (~tens of ms) responses reveal valid active accounts, which can then be targeted for password attacks or phishing.

These are the ONLY tests of GPKG MultiPolygon import with interior rings/holes, exterior-vs-hole line_type mapping, projected-CRS (LKS94) reprojection, and the 435-contour isobath pipeline — the class docstring claims exactly this complex coverage. Even if someone adds the data under the correctly spelled "curonian", the tests still skip because of the typo'd path.
  *Failure:* A regression in import_boundaries' interior-ring handling (e.g. holes emitted as line_type 1 instead of 2, or ring de-duplication breaking on MultiPolygon) ships with CI green -> Curonian Lagoon meshes — the lab's primary domain — are built with islands treated as water; nothing in CI or local runs can catch it, and the 10 skips are invisible among 2137 passes (no gate on skip count).

- **N53 · istod accepts sign characters after digits, silently misparsing values like '3.456-102'** — `src/utils/generic/convert.f90:211`
  In istod the minus/plus branches (lines 203-220) only test bexp/bsign, never bnumb/bdot, so a sign appearing AFTER digits is accepted as the number's leading sign and parsing continues. Verified with a compiled test: istod('12-3') returns 1 (success) with d=-123; istod('1.5-2') -> -1.52; istod('3.456-102') -> -3.456102. The form 'd.ddd-nnn' is exactly what Fortran E-format output produces when a 3-digit exponent overflows the field (E is dropped), and istod is the single number parser behind all STR-file parameter reads (nls_read_number), timeseries boundary/forcing files (ts_read_next_record via iscanf), and iscand/iscanf everywhere.
  *Failure:* A boundary-condition timeseries generated by another Fortran program contains a denormal-ish value printed as '3.456-102' (3-digit exponent, ~1e-102 i.e. essentially 0). SHYFEM silently reads it as -3.456102 instead of raising a parse error -> a physically wrong forcing value (e.g. -3.5 m water level or negative concentration) enters the simulation with no diagnostic.

- **N54 (adj. low) · off_read_record misaligned for version-3 offline files: ile/ilk records consumed twice** — `src/utils/shyutilmpi/io_off.f90:510`
  off_read_header accepts nvers >= 3 (lines 709-710). For nvers < 4 it reads the ile/ilk records itself to determine nlv (lines 729-737) and returns without repositioning the file. off_read_record then reads ileg/ilkg again at lines 510-512, which for a v3 file actually consumes the first data record (ut) reinterpreted as integers. All subsequent reads are shifted by two records: count_linear runs on garbage level counts (nlink/nline checks at 530-531 are skipped because v3 files have nlinkaux=nlineaux=0), and off_init_vertical/off_check_vertical receive garbage vertical indices.
  *Failure:* User runs the current model with a pre-2024 offline file (nvers=3, which the version check explicitly admits): if bvinit is false, off_init_vertical installs garbage layer counts and dlinear2vals unpacks data with wrong offsets -> crash in the best case, silently wrong hydrodynamic offline forcing in the worst; either way v3 files that the format check claims supported are unusable.

---

## 6. Per-subsystem health assessments

### Hydrodynamics & solvers
The zeta/momentum solve chain (hydro -> hydro_zeta -> system_solve -> hydro_transports_final) is structurally sound and the known F04 fix (PETSc serial assembly over nel_unique, skipping the OMP subset loop) is implemented correctly with owner-filtered RHS addition, so SPARSKIT/PETSc assembly parity holds in the normal semi-implicit path. The main weaknesses are in solver-failure handling and edge configurations: the PETSc/AmgX backends never check solver convergence (silently accepting diverged solves that SPARSKIT would abort on), the SPARSKIT path ignores ILU preconditioner error codes and keeps ~48 bytes/unknown of automatic stack arrays sized by the global node count on rank 0, and the explicit-scheme and vertical-momentum-advection code paths contain a deterministic error-stop-on-drying and an out-of-bounds array read respectively.

### Scalar transport (OMP/TVD)
The concentration/TVD/stability core follows the upstream algorithms and is sound in serial and MPI-only use, but the fork's own performance/cleanup remediations (commits 34ff6dd, 38469ab) converted per-call work arrays to `save`-cached ones without THREADPRIVATE protection, reintroducing exactly the class of OpenMP task data races the code's subset design was built to avoid: any OMP run combining temp/salt with tracers now shares (and in one case deallocates) solver state across concurrently executing scalar-advection tasks. In addition, the zero-pivot guard fix (6ba5312) leaves the serial tridiagonal solver in an inconsistent state on the guarded path, and several long-standing defects (intent(in) load write-back, non-conservative chapra settling, unguarded TVD divisions, MPI collectives from task context under MPI_THREAD_FUNNELED) affect mass conservation and hybrid-parallel correctness.

### Main loop & restart
The main-loop/init code (shyfem_subs.f90) and .shy output path are structurally careful (restart before setup_time re-init, master-only file opens with broadcast of output state), but the time module femtime carries a fossil integer `it` that is frozen at itanf while still being consumed by live lagrangian physics, silently disabling particle decay/mortality/connectivity. The restart subsystem checks nkn/nel/nlv but is weak on everything else: no iostat past the first header (truncated files abort instead of falling back), vertical layer geometry from the file is read but never validated, restart write hooks for simple-sediment exist but are unwired, and k-eps turbulence state is never saved. The .shy write error path uses master-only bare stop between MPI collectives, turning a disk-full into a cluster deadlock.

### Forcing & boundary conditions
The HEAD-commit (73e03b2) rewrites themselves are largely faithful: the iff_init goto-to-structured-if conversion in intp_fem_file.f90 preserves semantics exactly, and the vonkarman_dp import in meteo_forcing.f90 is correct. However, ww3.f90 (not compiled in the default build, so untested) carries a wrong-science radiation-stress argument swap and several ineffective/undefined-state patterns that the commit's stop-to-abort remediation did not address, and the meteo wind-drag/stress paths have unguarded calm-wind divisions that SIGFPE under the default -ffpe-trap build. The interpolation infrastructure (intp_fem_file.f90) is mature but silently disables its missing-data safety net for 3D regular grids and relies on bare stop in rank-divergent MPI paths.

### Ecological models
The weutro subsystem is in good shape after the 2026-06 hardening: the reaction-kernel and KAWIND/KAHYDRA GOTO removals are correct and were validated bit-for-bit, the euler positivity floor (Phase 1 C5) and MPI-safe aborts are in place, and the eco restart (e/es/esh/eul plus deterministic re-seeding of eseed/ulseed) is complete and symmetric with the skip path. The mercury subsystem is the weak side: its sediment integrator (merc_euler_sed) never got the positivity floor that weutro received, its sibling reactor files still contain bare `stop`s that F09 does not cover, and the claurent-OGS sediment-transport kernel divides by solids concentrations with no zero-guard. No regressions were found in the light-limitation path beyond the already-known F08/F30 (the C2 between-layer attenuation is a deliberate, consistent workaround, not a new double-count) and no new correctness bug was introduced by the intent()/GOTO/settling/NUTLIM refactors.

### MPI layer (shympi)
The shympi layer's core ghost-exchange and collective machinery is structurally sound: ghost-list pairing across ranks is validated at setup (ghost_exchange exchanges and cross-checks external node/element numbers), exchange sequences are posted in identical global order on all ranks (no deadlock topology found), and the recently added exchange_and_sum/min/max element-partition routines are currently dead code behind a hardwired shympi_partition_on_elements()=.false. The real weaknesses are in the abort/exit-status paths (success is reported as MPI_ABORT code 33 in both real and dummy modules), global-mesh-sized automatic stack arrays in the MPI setup path that will SIGSEGV on large basins, and a regression from HEAD commit 73e03b2 where the newunit= conversion silently disables all my_unit>0 debug guards; dummy-vs-real interface parity also has several latent gaps.

### Generic utilities
The generic/shyutil utility layer is mature legacy code that is mostly sound, but the review found one wrong-science bug (spherical->cartesian projection setup uses half the coordinate range instead of the midpoint, distorting all derived cartesian distances used by the wave module), plus silent misparse defects in the core string-to-number parser (istod) that every STR/timeseries read goes through. Error propagation is inconsistent across file readers (some return ierr, some stop, some abort on EOF), and the legacy version-3 offline-file read path is misaligned. Date/time core (dts/iso8601) is largely correct with only minor dead-code and overflow gaps.

### Fortran tools
src/tools/ is functional for the mainstream shyelab/femelab conversion paths, but several supported side modes are broken or silently wrong: -vorticity writes garbage/empty output, -write/-condense compute with the wrong array stride on mixed 2D/3D FEM files (files shyelab itself produces), extelab's hydro statistics use a stale/uninitialized buffer, and nc2fem emits internally inconsistent vertical headers for depth axes starting at 0. Fixed-form 72-column truncation affects only trailing comments (no code loss); array-bounds issues exist in the shy record reader (zeta records), and in shybas interpolation scratch arrays, and shybas interpolation mode 3 is entirely dead code that always aborts.

### C tools
The src/tools C sources are legacy single-author grid/mesh/postscript utilities (mostly 1990s vintage) that parse untrusted .grd mesh files and command-line filenames with no input hardening: fixed 80-byte filename buffers, sprintf %f into 20-byte buffers, unchecked hash-lookup results, and integer counts from atoi feeding malloc. Most are latent crashes/overflows reachable via crafted mesh files or long argv, comparable in class to the already-known F12/F39/F40/F43 items but in additional, unflagged files. The strongest issue is a NULL-pointer dereference in intgrd's depth interpolation that fires on well-formed input in the tool's normal workflow.

### Build system & scripts
The build plumbing is healthier than typical legacy Fortran projects — recursivemake propagates sub-make failures (exit 7), .PHONY coverage is thorough, and HEAD's new check_mpi_vendor target genuinely closes the Intel-MPI trap for the main `fem` path. However, the top-level Makefile carries dangerous bit-rot: the `petsc` convenience target silently delivers the wrong solver binary due to symlink semantics, several advertised targets (regress, nograph, compat, publish) reference directories deleted in the repo restructure, and the Dockerfile predates the switch to an MPI-by-default Rules.make so it can no longer build or run. The documented `MPI=true`/`OMP=false` build flags (used verbatim in CI) are consumed by nothing in the build system.

### UI security
The auth/authz core is generally sound and fail-closed: mutation gates (editor_denied_reason, check_project_access), admin authorization (uses server-validated current_user(), never the spoofable client-pushed user_role signal), and WS identity (256-bit server-minted _wsauth tokens delegating to session validation) all resist the obvious spoofing/escalation vectors, and I confirmed there is no HIGH authz bypass in the current code. The remaining issues are in the per-user confinement layer added by PR#29: a `.` username collapses the sandbox to the whole data root, and the confine_path boundary now excludes the shared work_dir where the bootstrapped tutorial project (and any pre-#29 project) still lives, making them unreachable because the intended relocation migration is dead code. Plus a login timing oracle enabling username/active-status enumeration.

### UI services
The services layer is broadly hardened (quota/traversal guards, DB retention, preflight fixes), but the job lifecycle has structural gaps: cancelling a job never kills the spawned shyfem/mpirun process, any WebSocket disconnect auto-cancels running jobs, server restarts leave phantom RUNNING rows that cleanup permanently excludes, and output-file discovery is glob-based, making workflow chaining pick arbitrary or stale files. Project export/import still do multi-GB CPU/disk work synchronously on the Shiny event loop, and the HEAD-73e03b2 CRS hardening introduced a small regression for pyproj-less deployments.

### UI pages & components
The pages/, app.py, and components/ scope is generally well-hardened: every disk-mutating handler routes through the fail-closed editor_denied_reason / identity_denied_reason / job_*_denied_reason gates using the server-validated WS identity (never the spoofable client role signal), all dynamic per-item reactive handlers use idempotent dedup sets, connect-time Shiny.setInputValue is correctly deferred inside fetch().then/setTimeout (no ProtocolError), render.ui outputs are top-level, and MapWidget IDs use module.resolve_id per the documented pattern. Two real functional defects surfaced: a reactive mutate-in-place bug that silently breaks the boundary editor's add/import, and a dead restart-file wiring in the Run page that silently discards restart selections.

### UI data layer
The DB layer is in decent shape: a build-and-diff of the full Alembic chain vs Base.metadata.create_all shows no material schema drift (only cosmetic ordering/constraint-name differences), SQLite FK enforcement is on, delete_user cleans or NULLs every referencing table, and service-level session handling consistently commits/rolls back/closes. The serious problems are concentrated in bootstrap and job persistence: init_db's Alembic branch is dead code (wrong alembic.ini path), so existing databases are never migrated or stamped by the app; and the jobs table has restart-lifecycle gaps — immortal zombie RUNNING rows, an output_files column that is never written or restored, and a no-commit path when a session factory is injected. Retention is now wired for jobs/sessions/audit but workflows have none, and the new cleanup code runs blocking DB+disk I/O on the event loop with timezone-mixed cutoffs.

### UI tests & CI
The UI test suite is in strong shape overall: 2137 unit tests pass in ~29s, the AST-based access-control locks (guard presence, polarity, ordering, unconditionality) are genuinely hard to bypass, source-lock strings were verified to still match production code, and sentinel tests guard the skip-prone E2E hooks. The real weaknesses are silent coverage holes rather than broken tests: an entire integration class (10 tests, including a brand-new regression test added in HEAD commit 73e03b2) is permanently skipped because its data directory never existed; a conftest-global SQLite PRAGMA listener quietly defeats the tests that claim to pin production FK enforcement; and CI has structural gaps — the MPI job never executes the binary it builds (this repo's own documented "compiles but crashes at MPI_Init" trap), the Docker job never builds the runtime stage, and the implicit-none ratchet carries 31 slots of stale slack.

### HEAD remediation commit 73e03b2
Commit 73e03b2 is largely sound: the ZIP import/export hardening is well-tested (the new per-project-dir traversal check, streaming extraction, and size limits all verified passing), the intp_fem_file GOTO removal faithfully preserves semantics, and the physical-constant swaps are numerically identical. However, the remediation introduced one real functional regression — switching the MPI debug file to open(newunit=) yields a negative unit that silently defeats every `my_unit > 0` guard in mpi_ghost/mpi_basin, gutting the very MPI diagnostics the commit claims to improve — plus an overzealous zip-bomb ratio heuristic that can reject the app's own legitimate exports, a new CRS regression test that never runs (placed in a class skipped because its data dir does not exist in the repo), and several incomplete-fix gaps (silent symlink drops on export, missing-CRS datasets still silently unprojected, PETSc target and non-"intel"-path Intel MPI escaping the new vendor check).

## 7. Recommended fix order

1. **Revert or thread-harden the `save`-cached work arrays** in `concentration.f90` / `concentration_omp.f90` (N01, N09, N10) — simplest correct fix is reverting `34ff6dd`/`38469ab` to per-call allocatables (the "caching" is a no-op in `conz3d_omp` anyway since the arrays are still deallocated every call); alternatively `!$OMP THREADPRIVATE`. Also resolve the MPI-from-tasks THREAD_FUNNELED violation (N11).
2. **Check PETSc convergence** (N04): `KSPSetErrorIfNotConverged` or explicit `KSPGetConvergedReason` + `shympi_abort` — restores parity with SPARSKIT's hard stop.
3. **UI job lifecycle** (N13, N14): terminate the subprocess on cancel; stop auto-cancelling jobs on WS disconnect; reconcile phantom RUNNING rows (N46).
4. **`init_db` Alembic path fix** (N12) — existing installs are never migrated/stamped by the app.
5. **femtime `it` freeze** (N05) and wind-stress calm-point guards (N03, and hersbach_cd N20).
6. **Build system truthfulness** (N02 `make petsc`, N19 inert `MPI=true/OMP=false` flags, N16 Dockerfile) — these mislead every downstream user.
7. Then work the remediation-scoreboard 'open' tail in priority order: MPI bare-stops (F07/F11/F27/F38), mercury hygiene (F09/F10/F31), C-tools memory safety (F12 et al.), UI F14/F16/F17/F25.
8. **Amend CLAUDE.md's "Allocation caching" pattern** with an explicit warning: never apply to routines invoked from concurrent OMP tasks without THREADPRIVATE.
